I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`, but I didn't check them against the Q2 reference values. The project rules in `CLAUDE.md` say not to re-run results or compare them with reference values, so I submitted the first output as is. That means I don't know yet whether my reading of the definitions reproduces your Q2 numbers.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net revenue / its net revenue | enterprise / 326,942,935 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 249 |
| c. Category with the highest net revenue / its net revenue | acc / 322,257,174 |
| d. Month with the highest net revenue | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u116@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 236 |
| g. Average net revenue per order | 714,077 |
| h. Growth from August to September | 21.3% |

The data had a few quirks, and I made these calls on them:
- **Segment labels:** they had stray spaces and inconsistent capitals (`" consumer"`, `"Enterprise "`, `SMB`), so I trimmed them and made them lowercase before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** there are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails, and copies with the same email sometimes have different segments. For b, e and f I counted one customer per email. For a, I used the segment on the specific customer record attached to each order.
- **Refunds:** the definition says to take the discounted unit price, round it down to the won, then multiply by the refunded quantity. That's what I did, and I subtracted the result from each line's amount.

If any of those calls doesn't match how the Q2 values were produced, b, e, f or a could change. The next step would be to run the same logic on Q2 and compare, but that would go against the `CLAUDE.md` rule.
